rules.title: Senate divisions
rules.citation: Constitution Act, 1867, s. 22 (four divisions of 24 senators, with Newfoundland and the territories added)
rules.detail: The Senate is built from four equal divisions of provinces. A region that spans two divisions has no seat count that follows from the text.

rules.title: The 7/50 amending formula
rules.citation: Constitution Act, 1982, s. 38(1) (resolutions of two-thirds of the provinces with at least half the population)
rules.detail: Two-thirds of the units, holding at least half the population, can amend the constitution. With a different number of units, the threshold is a different set of people.

rules.title: Equalization
rules.citation: Constitution Act, 1982, s. 36(2) (equalization payments so provinces can provide reasonably comparable services at reasonably comparable levels of taxation)
rules.detail: Equalization measures fiscal capacity per person against the national average. Redrawing the units moves the average and changes who is below it.

rules.title: Quebec's asymmetry
rules.citation: Constitution Act, 1867, ss. 94, 133 and Constitution Act, 1982, s. 59 (Quebec's civil law, its legislature and its language guarantees)
rules.detail: Quebec's civil law, language guarantees and opt-outs attach to Quebec as a unit. A set that cuts Quebec into pieces has to say which piece they attach to.

rules.title: Territorial status
rules.citation: Northwest Territories Act, S.C. 2014, c. 2, s. 2; Yukon Act, S.C. 2002, c. 7; Nunavut Act, S.C. 1993, c. 28 (territories are created by Parliament, not by the constitutional amending formula)
rules.detail: The territories exist by federal statute and can be changed by Parliament alone; provinces cannot. A region joining territory to province mixes the two.

rules.title: The senatorial floor on Commons seats
rules.citation: Constitution Act, 1867, s. 51A (no province has fewer Commons seats than senators)
rules.detail: The floor keeps small provinces over-represented in the Commons. It is written for provinces as they are; new units of very different size change who it protects.
